profile.address: 565 Metro Place South, Suite 300, Dublin, OH 43017
profile.reading: DartPoints operates an edge colocation data center at 565 Metro Place South, Suite 300, in Dublin, Ohio, part of the greater Columbus metro area, under the company code CMH01 referencing the Columbus airport designation. DartPoints is a real, Dallas, Texas-headquartered colocation and interconnection company that describes its strategy as bringing enterprise-grade data center infrastructure to secondary and tertiary US markets rather than the largest metro hubs. This Dublin facility traces its origin to Metro Data Centers, a Central Ohio-focused carrier-neutral colocation provider that DartPoints acquired on October 28, 2020, in a deal DartPoints' chief executive Scott Willis described as executing the company's strategy for regional growth aimed at improving interconnectivity, a description corroborated by independent private-equity trade coverage of the transaction. The facility spans 40,000 total square feet with a 5,900-square-foot data hall, drawing 3 megawatts of utility power against a 345-kilowatt critical IT load, cooled by 240 tons of N+1 redundant capacity, and hosting 11 on-site network providers offering connectivity from 1 to 100 gigabits. DartPoints itself has been backed first by Astra Capital Management, which took a majority investment position in May 2020 to fund a buy-and-build acquisition strategy, and more recently by NOVA Infrastructure, which made a strategic growth investment announced around April 2025 alongside Orion Infrastructure Capital in a deal reported at more than 250 million dollars combined, with Astra retaining a minority stake. DartPoints markets itself company-wide as SOC 2 and PCI compliant, though this specific facility page uses only general "AICPA SOC-compliant" language rather than citing a specific SOC 2 Type II report, and no Uptime Institute Tier certification level is stated for this building. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed.

reading.body:
DartPoints Dublin is a 3 MW colocation facility operated by DartPoints. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this IT load represents roughly 75 racks. The facility is certified for SOC 2 Type II compliance.

DartPoints operates across Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets, positioning itself as AI-ready infrastructure outside major metropolitan centers. The company received strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025 and maintains 11 facilities across Louisiana, Ohio, Indiana, North Carolina, and South Carolina. This geographic spread reflects a deliberate strategy to place compute capacity in secondary markets, where grid constraints and real estate costs differ substantially from coastal tech hubs. For AI workloads seeking colocation rather than hyperscale build-to-suit models, regional operators like DartPoints become relevant to the broader compute distribution question.

The data provided does not include total campus capacity, power source, water source, cooling technology, or grid interconnection details. No tenant names or workload types are disclosed. The 3 MW figure is the only publicly available operational metric for this facility. Without information on grid connection points, regional power availability, or whether the facility operates at stated capacity, this single number cannot answer whether regional data centers are becoming constrained by power access or whether they represent genuine alternatives to coastal colocation markets.
